transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Zoe Ramirez (Redwood CSM), Sonia Kapoor (NexaHealth Head of AI), Ethan Morales (Platform), Priya Singh (Security), Tom Reynolds (PM)

Summary (auto): quick check-in on onboarding progress, VPC/access items still pending, plan for benchmark run next week, security questions around KMS and log retention.

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick rol l call — who we got with us?
[00:12] Sonia Kapoor: hi yes this is sonia, i'm head of ai at nexahealth, joining from boston.
[00:18] Ethan Morales: ethan here, i'll be doing the infra bits.
[00:21] Priya Singh: priya from security.
[00:24] Tom Reynolds: tom, product.
[00:26] Maya Patel: awesome. liam and zoe are on from our side — liam's leading the bench runs, zoe will coordinate onboarding.
[00:35] Liam Chen: hey all. small note, my wifi might dip, i'll rejoin if i drop.
[00:40] Zoe Ramirez: hey all, good to meet you.

[02:05] Maya Patel: okay quick agenda: 1) access & env readiness, 2) perf/benchmark plan, 3) security/compliance Qs, 4) next steps. sound good?
[02:13] Sonia Kapoor: yes, that's good. we mostly want to get the dedicated pilot running next week.

[04:01] Ethan Morales: we've created a test VPC, but we haven't done peering yet. question — does redwood need inbound rules or just outbound to your control plane?
[04:20] Liam Chen: great question. for the private deployment we ask for egress to the control plane on port 443 for telemetry and management, and then we set up a private peering for the model traffic — so a couple of routes and a specific security group. i will send the exact CIDR recommendations.
[04:38] Priya Singh: and for keys — we want to bring our KMS, is that supported in the private deployment?
[04:45] Maya Patel: yes we support customer-managed keys, K M S integrations — for on-prem or private V P C we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. we'll include the KMS doc.

[06:10] Tom Reynolds: timeline question — if we get peering done Monday, could we run the benchmark Wednesday?
[06:18] Liam Chen: probably yes, assuming the service account and IAM bits are in place. the bench itself takes a few hours to run and then we need to analyze logs.
[06:30] Maya Patel: we'll aim for wed 8/26 for the run, liam will own.

[08:00] Sonia Kapoor: on the perf side, our target is p95 latency under 250ms for short prompts (~64 tokens) and throughput of ~60 rps for the demo workload. is that realistic?
[08:20] Liam Chen: rough ballpark, yes with a dedicated rp pool and quantized model we can get there — but it depends on sequence lengths and batching. also need to confirm the model variant; some open models hit higher latency.
[08:36] Maya Patel: one more caveat — we often see tradeoff between cost and latency; if you want lower cost we can recommend batching + quantization; but if latency SLO is primary we lean smaller batch sizes and maybe a different model.

[10:00] Ethan Morales: we're planning to use an internal transformer model for now, but open to the redwood curated models. how do we pick?
[10:12] Liam Chen: we usually run compatibility checks and perf profiles. liam: we'll run a quick eval with your test payloads and recommend a model + quantization profile.
[10:24] Sonia Kapoor: ok, please include quality regression check — we can't sacrifice accuracy.

[12:05] Maya Patel: security stuff — priya, what are your main blockers?
[12:11] Priya Singh: audit logs retention and key separation. we need to understand what logs redwood stores in-host versus what we must forward to our SIEM. also need SOC2 artifacts and an ISO checklist.
[12:22] Zoe Ramirez: we'll attach our SOC2 summary, and a log retention guide — note sometimes the transcription has typos but the docs are canonical.
[12:35] Priya Singh: also want clarity on RBAC and SSO — we use SAML with Okta.
[12:40] Maya Patel: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC. i'll put the SSO walkthrough in the pack.

[14:00] Tom Reynolds: any blockers on the data path? we plan not to persist PHI in the test workload but want to be sure of network isolation.
[14:12] Liam Chen: with dedicated pools + VPC peering you get network isolation; we can disable external egress from the workers and only allow routes to your internal stores.

[15:50] Sonia Kapoor: quick nit — in the docs i saw mention of "KV cache" management, is that something we need to configure?
[16:00] Liam Chen: the KV cache (sometimes shows up as K V cache in auto transcripts) is managed by the runtime; for many request patterns you can enable prefix caching to reduce cost. we'll show recommended settings after we see the request distribution.

[18:10] Maya Patel: ok onboarding status check — zoe, what have we completed?
[18:16] Zoe Ramirez: checklist: account created, service principal provisioned but pending permissions, sample prompts uploaded, test VPC exists but peering not done, security questionnaire partly answered. so roughly 60% done.

[20:00] Ethan Morales: about permissions — we tried the service account but got 403 when calling the control plane API. any ideas?
[20:12] Liam Chen: likely missing the role to access the model endpoint or missing the signing key. i'll send a troubleshooting snippet.

[22:00] Sonia Kapoor: on billing, we need a clearer view of unit cost for dedicated vs hosted, our finance team will ask.
[22:12] Maya Patel: i'll attach a simple cost model spreadsheet — it shows per-token and per-hour reserved capacity math, plus an example for your workload.

[24:00] Tom Reynolds: question on fallbacks — if a dedicated node goes down, does redwood auto-failover to hosted models?
[24:12] Liam Chen: yes we support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in hosted pool; you can configure fallback tiers and cost/latency tradeoffs. we'll include an example policy.

[26:00] Priya Singh: around audit logs — how long do you keep request logs and are they encrypted at rest?
[26:12] Zoe Ramirez: logs are encrypted at rest, retention depends on plan and can be pulled into your SIEM; default retention is 90 days for hosted, configurable for private. we'll add the full policy.

[28:00] Sonia Kapoor: ok good. on success criteria we want: 1) end-to-end demo with 60 rps and p95 < 250ms, 2) security sign-off, 3) clear cost estimate.
[28:12] Maya Patel: noted — we'll focus on those as primary gates.

[30:00] Ethan Morales: timeline-wise, if bench goes well on 8/26 we can sign off the pilot week after.
[30:12] Maya Patel: sounds realistic.

[32:00] Liam Chen: one more tech detail — for quantization we recommend int8 on A100ish hardware but if you're on different infra we may adjust. please list your GPU family in the infra doc.
[32:25] Ethan Morales: we'll include that in the VPC doc.

[34:00] Tom Reynolds: any legal/procurement steps to be aware of before pilot?
[34:12] Zoe Ramirez: standard pilot MSA, limited data addendum if required; procurement will usually want the SOC2 and DPA.

[36:00] Maya Patel: recap — action items and next steps: maya will share security/compliance pack and cost model; liam will prepare bench script; ethan to provide networking creds; priya to send audit questions. target bench 2026-08-26.

[38:00] Sonia Kapoor: quick Q — can you share example dashboards for latency/cost?
[38:10] Liam Chen: yes we'll share links to the console dash and a sample perf csv.

[40:00] Tom Reynolds: thanks everyone, that's useful.
[40:10] Maya Patel: thanks team, we'll follow up with docs and schedule.
[40:20] Zoe Ramirez: thanks all.
[40:30] (call ends)
